published_prior_art.cite: GarciaStillmanSturmfels2005 and KahleRauhSullivant2017 supply CI-ideal/saturation machinery, not a cross-graph intervention-signature rational-positive separation theorem.
TehSadeghiSoo2025Robust gives a sufficient simultaneous-ID criterion; Perkovic2020MPDAG is complete only for one MPDAG.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 2 / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: SparseSIM-ID completeness is conditional on Theorem 1's rational-positive separation result; generic rational-point density is neither assumed nor claimed.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The common-circuit-or-rational-separator completeness claim is asserted for certified tied-sparsest inputs provided the effect-specific rational-positive separation theorem is established.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.2 is sufficient for simultaneous identification over SA-MPDAG families; Section 4.2 states that a necessity proof needs one density Markovian to all candidate graphs with unequal graphwise interventions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2-6, Theorem 3.6 and surrounding bucket-factorization discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper supplies a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion and truncated-factorization formula for one MPDAG.
IDGraphs partitions one MPDAG into subclasses with identified, pairwise distinct total-effect functionals and establishes minimality within that MPDAG.
The work gives a complete identification algorithm and graphical nonidentification characterization for a single PAG.
Discrete causal queries are compiled to polynomial programs; the method supplies sharp bounds and anytime-valid outer ranges for a declared causal model.
SP selects a sparsest permutation DAG under conditions weaker than faithfulness; it is a discovery method, not an effect-aware tie-resolution procedure.

source_verification_receipts.version: Handbook of Graphical Models chapter / arXiv:1705.07411
source_verification_receipts.locator: abstract and Sections 3.1, 3.3 as cited in the core
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The chapter treats primary decompositions of conditional-independence ideals and real-algebraic issues in graphical models.
The proposed resampling-and-screening construction unions graph-based intervals and gives asymptotic coverage for a fixed population-level causal effect after causal discovery.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make Theorem 1's first nontrivial step auditable on a parameterized nondegenerate tied-MEC family: prove or computationally certify that the exact-CI zero blocks and strict positivity can be retained while a failed signature remains nonzero. This would directly stress-test the rational-positive bridge rather than only its four-node endpoint.

State a full bit-complexity bound for computing the saturated real-radical normal forms and certificates, not only the subsequent rational-table enumeration count; this would turn SparseSIM-ID into an unambiguous constructive-decision result.

Add a positive equality-branch cross-MEC worked instance, alongside the present separator, and verify the cited 2005 journal version's exact Theorem 8 locator before relying on that theorem-number comparison.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with Theorem 1 retained as the focal open bridge and Theorem 2 explicitly conditioned on it; treat Theorem 3 as supporting inference rather than a novelty claim.
